title: React Redux Toolkit store slices selectors middleware and async workflows
concepts: Redux is a predictable shared-state architecture: events dispatch actions, reducers calculate the next immutable state, and subscribers select data for rendering.

Redux Toolkit is the standard approach for Redux logic. configureStore supplies sensible defaults, createSlice generates reducer and action behavior, and Immer lets reducer code express immutable updates with draft mutations.
Selectors encapsulate state lookups and derive minimal stored data into view-ready values. Memoized selectors cache calculations based on input identity.

Middleware extends dispatch for cross-cutting or asynchronous workflows. Thunks handle request lifecycles; listener middleware reacts to actions and state changes with cancellable async workflow helpers.

React-Redux connects the store to a component tree through Provider; useSelector subscribes to selected values and useDispatch sends actions. Hooks are the recommended component integration. connect() is marked deprecated as of React-Redux 9.3.0, remains functional, and is not planned for removal; legacy_connect is the non-deprecated alias for existing code that retains it.
Use normalized entity data and derive values instead of duplicating them. RTK Query is the purpose-built fetching and caching option and is outside this topic's bounded core Redux workflow inventory.
